inputs.name: Earlier diagnostic kernel for the visual pointer check

scenario: After a warm reboot, test physical HDMI, a bounded native KMS run, and a Qt/Vulkan resize workload with NPU activity. Record the visual pointer check from its separate earlier boot.
expected: KWin reports active PowerVR composition on physical HDMI. Native KMS completes the requested flips. The Qt window keeps presenting during resize and the fixed arithmetic tiles match their reference.
observed: After reboot on e29c9e337, KWin reported HDMI-A-1 and active OpenGL ES composition through Zink on PowerVR B-Series BXM-4-64 MC1. Native KMS completed 2000 flips in 126.671 s with Plasma stopped. A Qt/Vulkan window alternating between 640 × 480 and 960 × 640 reported 1534 frameSwapped signals in 116.872 s. Two independent CRTC polling intervals observed 731 and 761 framebuffer changes. DRM and DE reported zero errors after both runs. Two NPU runs during the desktop workload each verified 1024 arithmetic tiles. On this setup, disabling the KWin maximize effect reduced restore geometry latency by 63 to 317 ms in four paired comparisons. On the earlier a6f1c5c36 boot, the operator confirmed visible cursor motion using the Logitech receiver through ums and wsmouse.
limits: The board revision is unknown. The graphics DTB hash identifies the installed DTB.
The pointer movement was confirmed on a separate earlier boot. The current kernel source revision and image hash identify the reboot and bounded runtime tests.
The monitor refresh rate describes the HDMI mode. Qt swap signals and polled CRTC framebuffer changes are separate measurements.
The restore comparison applies to this setup. It measures reported window geometry, not optical latency.
Earlier diagnostic KMS tests encountered intermittent RCQ and TV0 retirement timeouts. Cold boot, hotplug and longer operation remain unqualified.
